name: Synthrex
description: Synthrex is a neuroplasticity amplifier that temporarily upregulates NMDA receptor sensitivity and synaptic growth factor expression, putting the brain into a state of heightened plasticity that mirrors the learning capacity of adolescence. During its window, new motor skills, languages, technical procedures, and conceptual frameworks are acquired 3-5x faster than baseline. It was developed for accelerated military operator training but leaked into civilian markets via Helix's licensing disputes.
effects: Reduced mental fatigue during intensive study
BCI-assisted learning feeds integrate more efficiently
side_effects: Regression of recently learned skills if dose is interrupted mid-acquisition
Emotional volatility — heightened plasticity affects emotional regulation too
Risk of acquiring bad habits as readily as good ones — poor training during a Synthrex window is very difficult to unlearn
cultural_context: Synthrex is the drug of certification mills and corporate fast-track programs — a 72-hour Synthrex-assisted immersion can produce competency that normally takes six months. Helix markets it carefully, aware that regulators watch it closely. On the street it's called 'Fast-track' and is used by Tier 2 workers trying to qualify for Tier 3 jobs without the time or money for formal education. The 'Hollow' — the 12-24 hours of mental emptiness after a heavy Synthrex cycle — is considered a badge of honor in hustle culture.
story_hooks: A the Gray Zone runner used bootleg Synthrex to learn a corporate security system's maintenance protocols — but the bad data they trained on is now deeply wired in, and a job goes wrong because of it

A Helix researcher discovers that Synthrex's military-grade formulation is being manufactured in a the Gray Zone lab — someone leaked the synthesis protocol, and people are going into 'the Hollow' and not coming out
A character needs to master a skill in 48 hours that should take years — and Synthrex is the only option, with a trainer who may or may not be teaching them correctly
